blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Glenbrooke North

items.t: Glenbrooke North is a mainland residential neighbourhood north of Queen's Park, around Glenbrook Ravine, Jamieson Court and Park Crescent. The City spells the name "Glenbrooke North" and lists it among its Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements.

Nearby areas: Queens Park (the Heritage Conservation Area) to the south, Sapperton to the east across McBride Boulevard, Massey Victory Heights beyond Sapperton, and Downtown / Uptown to the south-west. Identity note: Glenbrooke North is a real City-recognised neighbourhood name, but it is not a Heritage Conservation Area.

Parks and recreation: Glenbrook Ravine park and trail run through the area, and Queen's Park (arena, sportsplex, stadium, sports fields) sits at the south edge. The city's main aquatic centre, the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre, 65 East Sixth Avenue, is in Uptown. Library: Main Branch, New Westminster Public Library, 716 6th Avenue. Health care: Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street, in Sapperton, and Queens Park Care Centre, 315 McBride Blvd, at the Queen's Park edge.

Roads and transit: 8th Avenue, 8th Street and McBride Boulevard serve the area, linking south to Downtown and the Pattullo Bridge approach and north to East Columbia Street in Sapperton. No SkyTrain station is inside Glenbrooke North; the nearest are Columbia Station and Sapperton Station (Expo Line); TransLink routes 123 (New Westminster Station / Brentwood Station) and 102 (Victoria Hill / New Westminster Station) serve the north mainland corridors.
Schools: SD40 catchments are address-based. Howay Elementary (K–5), École Glenbrook Middle (6–8) and New Westminster Secondary (9–12).

Market context, labelled correctly: September 2026 SnapStats — Glenbrooke North sub-area detached inventory 17 / sales 2 (12% ratio) and "Condos & Townhomes" combined inventory 10 / sales 2 (20% ratio), a small sample in both segments; New Westminster community detached median $1,365,000 and condos & townhomes median $560,000.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Glenbrooke North

items.t: Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001: houses sit under the RS series (s.310) — RS-1 minimum site 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.), FSR 0.5; RM-1 (s.420) caps site coverage at 40% and density at 35 units per net acre / FSR 1.2 where designated.
Ravine / streamside diligence: Glenbrook Ravine is a watercourse corridor in the City Green Zone. Parks and Open Space.pdf
Heritage context (not a permit layer here): the Glenbrooke North / Queen's Park context work documents some of the city's oldest dwellings in this combined area.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Glenbrooke North ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

blocks.text: Good to know about Glenbrooke North

items.t: Old houses, no heritage permit layer: the combined Glenbrooke North / Queen's Park context work documents some of the city's oldest dwellings here, yet no HCA covers Glenbrooke North.

The ravine quietly shrinks lots: Glenbrook Ravine–edge lots can carry streamside setbacks that reduce buildable area below what the RS-1 site area suggests — the setback, not the zone minimum, is the binding number on those parcels, and it is lot-specific. Parks and Open Space.pdf

Glenbrooke North is a mainland residential neighbourhood north of Queen's Park, wrapped around Glenbrook Ravine, Jamieson Court and Park Crescent in New Westminster — the ravine, not a main road, is its organising feature.

Watch the spelling: the City spells the neighbourhood "Glenbrooke North" (with the second e) but the ravine, park and drive inside it are "Glenbrook" — Glenbrook Ravine Park, Glenbrook Drive — and the middle school is École Glenbrook Middle.

What adjoins it: the Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area to the south, Sapperton to the east across McBride Boulevard, Massey Victory Heights beyond Sapperton, and Downtown and Uptown to the south-west.

The stock is single-detached houses on quiet residential streets, and the combined Glenbrooke North / Queen's Park context work documents some of the oldest dwellings in the city in this area — age is a feature of the housing stock here, not an exception.
Queens Park Care Centre, a Fraser Health facility at 315 McBride Boulevard, sits at the Queen's Park edge of the area — the institutional neighbour on the area's south-east corner.

blocks.text: Glenbrooke North: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Glenbrook Ravine is a watercourse corridor in the City's Green Zone, so ravine-edge lots can carry streamside setbacks that reduce the buildable area — the setback for a specific lot is confirmed parcel by parcel with the City. Parks and Open Space.pdf
The area is documented in the City's Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements — context documentation is not the same as HCA protection, and it does not by itself restrict a renovation.

blocks.text: Glenbrooke North: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Glenbrook Ravine Park's listed address is 76 Jamieson Court, and its parking and washrooms are up at the nearby təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre, with limited accessible parking on Jamieson Court itself.

The ravine is actively restored by volunteers: the Glenbrook Ravine Restoration weed pulls, led by the Invasive Species Council of Metro Vancouver with City Parks and Recreation and New Westminster Environmental Partners, target Himalayan blackberry in the ravine's middle section.

Metro Vancouver's sewer work has closed ravine access points in turn — trail access via Kwantlen Court was closed for approximately two months and intermittently through the project, and the Jamieson Court trail entrance closed temporarily in February 2026 during site restoration — so which entrance is open changes with the project phase, not permanently.
The nearest library branch is the Main Branch of the New Westminster Public Library at 716 6th Avenue, south-west in Uptown.

Queen's Park — arena, sportsplex, stadium and sports fields — is at the area's south edge, so Glenbrooke North's arena and stadium access runs through the Queen's Park complex, not a facility of its own.

blocks.text: Glenbrooke North: development and new projects

items.t: Glenbrook Sewer Upgrade — Glenbrook Ravine Section, Metro Vancouver project in Glenbrook Ravine Park: upgrading the sewer and the diversion chamber that manages wet-weather flows, with two new maintenance holes, a new sewer pipe and a replacement gate in the diversion chamber.
Royal Columbian Hospital (RCH) Redevelopment, Sapperton — named once here; it is on the City's Projects On The Go list and its full entry belongs on the Sapperton page.

Queen's Park Artificial Turf Replacement Project — named once here; a City project at the Queen's Park complex on this area's south edge, listed among completed projects on the City's Projects On The Go list (as of November 3, 2026).

TransLink route 123 (New Westminster Station / Brentwood Station) and route 102 (Victoria Hill / New Westminster Station) serve the north mainland corridors around Glenbrooke North; the nearest SkyTrain stations are Columbia and Sapperton on the Expo Line.
McBride Boulevard is the area's spine: it links the neighbourhood south to Downtown and the Pattullo Bridge approach, and north to East Columbia Street in Sapperton.

Inside the neighbourhood, movement is the ravine trail system itself — entrances at Jamieson Court and via Kwantlen Court and Glenbrook Drive connect the streets above and below the ravine, and Metro Vancouver's project page is where current trail closures are posted.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot in Glenbrooke North?
faq.a: No verified one — no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata or presale lot offering was verified; the stock is established RS house lots and built strata.

faq.q: How small can a lot be, and can I split one?
faq.a: RS-1 sets a minimum site of 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.) with FSR 0.5; RM-1, where designated, caps coverage at 40% and density at FSR 1.2. Subdivision runs under Bylaw No. 7142, 2007, with Approving Officer approval and adequate servicing.

faq.q: What do RT-A and RT-B allow here?
faq.a: RT-A and RT-B are New Westminster's newer townhouse districts: a site needs at least 836.1 m² (9,000 sq. ft.) of site area, at least 20 m of frontage and lane access. Whether a particular Glenbrooke North lot is designated or zoned for townhouses is a question for City Planning.

faq.q: What does a ravine-edge lot need checked?
faq.a: Streamside setbacks — Glenbrook Ravine is a watercourse corridor in the City Green Zone and setbacks are lot-specific. Check them before promising additions. Parks and Open Space.pdf

faq.q: Which schools serve a Glenbrooke North address?
faq.a: Howay Elementary (Kindergarten to Grade 5), École Glenbrook Middle (Grades 6–8) and New Westminster Secondary (Grades 9–12).

faq.q: What is Glenbrook Ravine like to live beside?
faq.a: It is a City park and trail corridor running through the neighbourhood, with the park entrance at 76 Jamieson Court and further access points at Jamieson Court (south) and via Kwantlen Court and Glenbrook Drive. Metro Vancouver's Glenbrook Sewer Upgrade has been working in the ravine, with site restoration — irrigation, signage, new asphalt and planting — under way in 2026 and short temporary trail-entrance closures, so a home beside the ravine trades a green setting for periodic utility construction.

faq.q: How do I get to SkyTrain from Glenbrooke North?
faq.a: There is no station in the neighbourhood; the nearest are Columbia Station and Sapperton Station on the Expo Line. TransLink route 123 (New Westminster Station / Brentwood Station) and route 102 (Victoria Hill / New Westminster Station) serve the north mainland corridors around the area. In practice that makes Glenbrooke North a bus-or-drive-to-station neighbourhood, unlike the Downtown and Quay neighbourhoods at the stations themselves.

faq.q: Is Glenbrooke North inside the Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area?
faq.a: No — the HCA covers the Queen's Park neighbourhood to the south. Confirm any specific address with the City.
